title: Why people believe in conspiracy theories, with Karen Douglas, PhD

sentences.en: Over the past year, as COVID-19 rocketed around the world, conspiracy theories quickly followed.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，随着新冠疫情在全球迅速蔓延，阴谋论也随之甚嚣尘上。

sentences.en: Last spring, dozens of cell phone towers were set aflame across Europe amid conspiracy theories that the 5G towers were spreading COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 去年春天，欧洲各地发生了多起手机信号塔被纵火的事件，起因是有人散布阴谋论，称5G信号塔在传播新冠病毒。

sentences.en: In January, a Wisconsin pharmacist was charged with deliberately destroying hundreds of doses of the newly available COVID-19 vaccine
sentences.zh: 今年一月，威斯康星州一名药剂师因蓄意销毁数百剂刚上市的新冠疫苗而被起诉，

sentences.en: because he believed a conspiracy theory that the vaccine would change human DNA.
sentences.zh: 因为他相信了一个阴谋论，认为疫苗会改变人类的DNA。

sentences.en: And some people are asserting that the virus itself was engineered by the Chinese.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人声称，这种病毒本身就是中国人制造的。

sentences.en: These aren't the only conspiracy theories making inroads right now.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是目前唯一流行的阴谋论。

sentences.en: A September Pew Research Center survey found that more than half of Americans have heard at least a little about QAnon, the complicated web of pro-Trump conspiracy theories
sentences.zh: 皮尤研究中心九月份的一项调查发现，超过半数的美国人听说过“匿名者Q”（QAnon），这是一个复杂的亲特朗普阴谋论网络，

sentences.en: that originated on the message board 4chan.
sentences.zh: 它起源于留言板4chan。

sentences.en: In November, two candidates who voiced support for QAnon theories were elected to Congress.
sentences.zh: 十一月，两名公开支持“匿名者Q”理论的候选人当选为国会议员。

sentences.en: So how do conspiracy theories like these get started, and why do they persist?
sentences.zh: 那么，这类阴谋论是如何产生的？又为何能持续存在？

sentences.en: Who is most likely to believe them, and why?
sentences.zh: 什么样的人最容易相信它们？原因又是什么？

sentences.en: Is there any way to combat conspiracy theories once they're out there?
sentences.zh: 当阴谋论出现后，有什么办法可以反击吗？

sentences.en: And what are the consequences for individuals and societies when they spread?
sentences.zh: 当它们传播开来时，对个人和社会又会产生什么后果？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Karen Douglas, a professor of social psychology at the University of Kent in the UK.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是英国肯特大学的社会心理学教授凯伦·道格拉斯博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Douglas has spent more than a decade studying conspiracy theories, and she joins us to talk about their history, causes, and consequences.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯博士研究阴谋论已超过十年，今天她将与我们探讨阴谋论的历史、成因及其后果。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Douglas.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，道格拉斯博士。

sentences.en: Hi, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你好，金。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for your invitation.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: Hi, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: So let's start with a definition.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们先从定义开始。

sentences.en: That's always a good place to launch.
sentences.zh: 这总是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: What counts as a conspiracy theory?
sentences.zh: 什么才算阴谋论？

sentences.en: I gave a few examples in the introduction, but how do you define conspiracy theories in your research?
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中举了几个例子，但在您的研究中，您是如何定义阴谋论的？

sentences.en: What are their common characteristics?
sentences.zh: 它们有哪些共同特征？

sentences.en: Well, a conspiracy theory can normally be defined as a proposed plot carried out in secret, usually by a powerful group of people who have some kind of sinister goal,
sentences.zh: 嗯，阴谋论通常可以定义为一种秘密策划的阴谋，通常由一群拥有某种邪恶目标的有权势的人实施，

sentences.en: so something to gain from what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们能从自己的所作所为中获利。

sentences.en: And they usually don't have people's best interests at heart, usually their own interests at heart.
sentences.zh: 而且他们通常不会把公众的利益放在心上，往往只顾及自己的利益。

sentences.en: Some people think that the belief in conspiracy theories has been on the rise in recent years, fueled by social media.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为，近年来在社交媒体的推波助澜下，对阴谋论的信仰有所抬头。

sentences.en: But in a paper a few years ago, you concluded that wasn't necessarily true.
sentences.zh: 但您在几年前的一篇论文中得出结论，事实未必如此。

sentences.en: Instead, you found that conspiracy theories have always thrived during times of crisis and social upheaval, with examples going back as far as the burning of Rome
sentences.zh: 相反，您发现阴谋论在危机和社会动荡时期总是盛行，例子可以追溯到罗马大火时期，

sentences.en: while Nero was away, and that the last decade hasn't been particularly more conspiracy-prone than the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当时尼禄皇帝不在城中。过去十年里，人们并没有比过去更容易相信阴谋论。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that, and how do researchers measure this?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这一点吗？研究人员又是如何衡量这一点的？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Yes, it is definitely the case that conspiracy theories have always been with us.
sentences.zh: 是的，阴谋论一直伴随着我们，这绝对是事实。

sentences.en: Believing in conspiracy theories and being suspicious about the actions of others is in some ways quite an adaptive thing to do.
sentences.zh: 相信阴谋论并对他人行为保持怀疑，在某种程度上是一种相当具有适应性的行为。

sentences.en: We don't necessarily want to trust everybody and trust everything that's happening around us.
sentences.zh: 我们未必想要去信任每一个人，或者信任我们周围发生的一切。

sentences.en: And so they have always been with us.
sentences.zh: 所以它们一直伴随着我们。

sentences.en: And to some extent, people are all,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，人们都是，

sentences.en: I guess you could call everybody a conspiracy theorist, if you want to use that term, at one point or another.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你愿意用这个词的话，可以说每个人在某个时刻都是阴谋论者。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, they've always been there.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它们一直都在那里。

sentences.en: People have always believed in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 人们一直都相信阴谋论。

sentences.en: As far back as we can remember, people have been having these conspiracy beliefs and having these suspicions about the actions of hostile collectives of individuals.
sentences.zh: 从我们记事起，人们就一直持有这些阴谋论信仰，并对敌对群体个人的行为抱有怀疑。

sentences.en: This is just the way that we are wired up to some degree.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这就是我们的天性。

sentences.en: And in terms of how we measure the extent to which people believe in conspiracy theories, you can do this in a variety of different ways.
sentences.zh: 至于我们如何衡量人们相信阴谋论的程度，你可以通过多种不同的方式来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And as psychologists, as a social psychologist now, we would normally measure belief in conspiracy theories by simply asking people questions
sentences.zh: 作为心理学家，我现在是一名社会心理学家，我们通常会通过简单地询问人们问题来衡量对阴谋论的信仰，

sentences.en: about the extent to which they endorse a particular idea or the extent to which they believe a particular statement is true.
sentences.zh: 询问他们赞同某个特定观点的程度，或者他们认为某个特定陈述为真的程度。

sentences.en: And you can measure these sorts of beliefs on specific issues.
sentences.zh: 你可以针对具体问题来衡量这类信仰。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you want to know how much somebody believes in anti-vaccine conspiracy theories, then you can ask people to read a bunch of statements
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你想知道某人对反疫苗阴谋论的相信程度，那么你可以让人们阅读一系列陈述，

sentences.en: about anti-vaccine conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 关于反疫苗阴谋论的陈述。

sentences.en: So, for example, that pharmaceutical companies are hiding information about vaccine efficacy and safety.
sentences.zh: 例如，制药公司隐瞒了关于疫苗效力和安全性的信息。

sentences.en: And then you ask them how much they believe that statement or how much they agree with it, how much they think it's plausible.
sentences.zh: 然后你问他们有多相信这个陈述，或者他们有多同意它，有多认为它合理。

sentences.en: There are various different ways that you can do this.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过多种不同的方式来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And another way to kind of tap into what some would argue is an underlying tendency to just believe conspiracy theories more generally, you can ask more general questions
sentences.zh: 还有另一种方式可以触及一些人所说的更普遍的相信阴谋论的潜在倾向，你可以问一些更笼统的问题，

sentences.en: or ask people to rate the extent to which they believe in statements such as governments often hide secrets from people to suit their own ends.
sentences.zh: 或者让人们评估他们相信诸如“政府经常为了自己的目的而向民众隐瞒秘密”这类陈述的程度。

sentences.en: So more general notions of conspiracy like that.
sentences.zh: 所以就是诸如此类更普遍的阴谋论概念。

sentences.en: So we'll just ask participants to read these sort of statements and rate the extent to which they agree with them, usually on a scale from I strongly disagree
sentences.zh: 我们会让参与者阅读这些陈述，并评估他们赞同的程度，通常采用从“我非常不同意”

sentences.en: to I strongly agree, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 到“我非常同意”这样的量表。

sentences.en: And then usually what we will do is come up with an average conspiracy belief measure or score, I suppose, total for each individual.
sentences.zh: 然后我们通常会得出一个平均的阴谋论信仰衡量标准或分数，我想，是每个人的总分。

sentences.en: And then we'll look for associations between that kind of belief and various other psychological factors as well.
sentences.zh: 接着我们也会寻找这种信仰与其他各种心理因素之间的关联。

sentences.en: So the belief is generally always out there.
sentences.zh: 所以这种信仰通常一直都存在。

sentences.en: The conspiracies may change over time.
sentences.zh: 阴谋论的内容可能会随时间而改变。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering, have there been times in history that you've seen when conspiracy theories have spiked?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，在历史上你是否观察到过阴谋论激增的时期？

sentences.en: Um, not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不一定。

sentences.en: It's not something I really research in my own, in my own studies.
sentences.zh: 这不是我个人研究中真正去探讨的内容。

sentences.en: But naturally, a lot of people are very concerned at the moment that we're seeing a bit of a spike in believing conspiracy theories
sentences.zh: 但自然地，很多人目前非常担心我们正看到阴谋论信仰出现了一些激增，

sentences.en: with the whole coronavirus situation and also in the USA with the recent presidential election.
sentences.zh: 伴随着整个新冠疫情的情况，以及在美国最近的总统选举中也是如此。

sentences.en: And I guess time will tell if we, if conspiracy theories have, I guess, been on the rise in this particular point in time compared to times in the past or times in the future.
sentences.zh: 我想时间会证明，与过去或未来的时期相比，在这个特定的时间点，阴谋论是否真的在增加。

sentences.en: But there is definitely quite a lot of concern that conspiracy theories are on the rise.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，人们非常担心阴谋论正在抬头。

sentences.en: It's difficult for me to say whether or not they are because I don't really have the data to support, you know, one way or another.
sentences.zh: 我很难说它们是否真的在增加，因为我确实没有数据来支持这一方或那一方的观点。

sentences.en: But I think that it is definitely the case that even if we can't say for sure that social media has increased conspiracy theories,
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以肯定的是，即使我们不能确定社交媒体是否增加了阴谋论，

sentences.en: it's certainly changed the way in which people access this information, the ways in which they share this information.
sentences.zh: 它无疑改变了人们获取这些信息的方式，以及他们分享这些信息的方式。

sentences.en: And also I feel that in many cases for people who do have, I guess, an underlying tendency to believe in a particular conspiracy theory
sentences.zh: 而且我也觉得，在许多情况下，对于那些确实有某种潜在倾向去相信特定阴谋论，

sentences.en: or conspiracy theories in general, it's much easier for people to find this sort of information now than it ever has been before.
sentences.zh: 或者普遍相信阴谋论的人来说，现在比以往任何时候都更容易找到这类信息。

sentences.en: And people can become consumed by this information.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会被这些信息所吞噬。

sentences.en: They can only seek out this information online so they can go to particular sources, disregard other sources that kind of contradict their views so that they end up, if anything,
sentences.zh: 他们可能只会在线寻找这些信息，从而只去特定的来源，无视其他与他们观点相左的来源，以至于他们最终，如果非要说的话，

sentences.en: their attitudes about these particular alleged conspiracy theories or alleged conspiracies, rather, sorry, can become even more polarised
sentences.zh: 他们对这些所谓的阴谋论，或者说所谓的阴谋，抱歉，他们的态度可能会变得更加极端，

sentences.en: so people's attitudes might become stronger.
sentences.zh: 所以人们的态度可能会变得更加强烈。

sentences.en: So I guess what I'm trying to say is that even if we don't have evidence that conspiracy theorising has increased, I think that, and time will tell
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我想表达的是，即使我们没有证据表明阴谋论的传播有所增加，但我认为，时间会证明

sentences.en: whether or not that's true, I do think that people's attitudes have become stronger as a result of interacting and sharing and consuming this information
sentences.zh: 这是否属实，我确实认为人们在接触、分享和消费这些信息后，态度变得更加强烈了，

sentences.en: on social media and on the internet generally.
sentences.zh: 无论是在社交媒体上还是在整个互联网上。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering, I think I read that there may have been a measurable increase in conspiracy theory theorising around the turn of the 20th century
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，我记得我读到过，在20世纪之交，阴谋论的传播似乎有可衡量的增加，

sentences.en: because of the Industrial Revolution, and then also around the end of the Second World War and the beginning of the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 这是因为工业革命，然后是在第二次世界大战结束和冷战开始的时候。

sentences.en: So is that accurate?
sentences.zh: 那么这准确吗？

sentences.en: I think I have come across one study which suggests that that's the case.
sentences.zh: 我想我确实看到过一项研究，暗示情况确实如此。

sentences.en: But yeah, the evidence is really quite limited and only drawn from a particular type of sources like letters to newspapers and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 但确实，证据非常有限，而且仅来自特定类型的来源，比如给报纸的信件之类的东西。

sentences.en: So it's really difficult to tell, but it does make sense to me that there would have been particular periods in history that conspiracy theories would have been more prominent.
sentences.zh: 所以真的很难说，但对我来说，历史上确实存在某些时期，阴谋论会更加突出，这在逻辑上是讲得通的。

sentences.en: And personally, I think we might be in one of those periods right now.
sentences.zh: 而且我个人认为，我们现在可能正处于这样的时期之一。

sentences.en: Let's talk a little bit about the psychological factors that motivate people to believe in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈促使人们相信阴谋论的心理因素。

sentences.en: I know you've laid out in your research three areas that you call epistemic, existential, and social motives.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在研究中提出了三个领域，你称之为认知动机、存在动机和社会动机。

sentences.en: Can you explain what they are, what those terms mean?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下它们是什么，这些术语意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: We argue that people are drawn to conspiracy theories in order to satisfy or in an attempt to satisfy three important psychological motives.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，人们被阴谋论所吸引，是为了满足或试图满足三个重要的心理动机。

sentences.en: And the first of these motives are epistemic motives.
sentences.zh: 第一个动机是认知动机。

sentences.en: And I guess in a nutshell, epistemic motives really just refer to the need for knowledge and certainty.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，认知动机实际上指的就是对知识和确定性的需求。

sentences.en: And I guess the motive or desire to have information.
sentences.zh: 也就是获取信息的动机或欲望。

sentences.en: And when something major happens, when a big event happens, people naturally want to know why that happened.
sentences.zh: 当发生重大事件时，人们自然想知道为什么会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: They want an explanation and they want to know the truth.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一个解释，想要知道真相。

sentences.en: But they also want to feel certain of that truth.
sentences.zh: 但他们也想对那个真相感到确定。

sentences.en: And some psychological evidence suggests that people are drawn to conspiracy theories when they do feel uncertain, either in specific situations or more generally.
sentences.zh: 一些心理学证据表明，当人们感到不确定时，无论是在特定情况下还是在更广泛的层面上，他们都会被阴谋论所吸引。

sentences.en: And there are other epistemic reasons why people believe in conspiracy theories as well in relation to this sort of need for knowledge and certainty.
sentences.zh: 除了这种对知识和确定性的需求外，人们相信阴谋论还有其他认知方面的原因。

sentences.en: So people with lower levels of education tend to be drawn to conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 受教育程度较低的人往往更容易被阴谋论所吸引。

sentences.en: And we don't argue that's because people are not intelligent.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是说这是因为人们不够聪明。

sentences.en: It's simply that they haven't been allowed to have or haven't been given access to the tools to allow them to differentiate between good sources and bad sources or credible sources
sentences.zh: 只是他们没有被允许拥有，或者没有获得相应的工具，让他们能够区分好的来源和坏的来源，或者说可信的来源

sentences.en: and non-credible sources.
sentences.zh: 和不可信的来源。

sentences.en: So they're looking for that knowledge and certainty, but not necessarily looking in the right places.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是在寻找那种知识和确定性，但未必是在正确的地方寻找。

sentences.en: And the second set of motives we would call existential motives.
sentences.zh: 第二组动机我们称之为存在动机。

sentences.en: And really, they just refer to people's needs to be or to feel safe and secure in the world
sentences.zh: 它们实际上指的就是人们在他们所居住的世界中需要感到安全和可靠，

sentences.en: that they live in and also to feel that they have some kind of power or autonomy over the things that happen to them as well.
sentences.zh: 同时也需要感到他们对发生在自己身上的事情有一定的掌控力或自主权。

sentences.en: So again, when something happens, people don't like to feel powerless.
sentences.zh: 所以同样，当事情发生时，人们不喜欢感到无能为力。

sentences.en: They don't like to feel out of control.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢感到失去控制。

sentences.en: And so reaching to conspiracy theories might, I guess, at least allow people to feel that
sentences.zh: 所以转向阴谋论可能，我想，至少能让人们感觉到

sentences.en: they have information that at least explains why they don't have any control over this situation.
sentences.zh: 他们掌握的信息至少能解释为什么他们对这种情况没有任何控制权。

sentences.en: And research has shown that people who do feel powerless and disillusioned do tend to gravitate more towards conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，那些感到无能为力和幻灭的人确实倾向于更多地转向阴谋论。

sentences.en: And the final set of motives we would call social motives, and those refer to people's desire
sentences.zh: 最后一组动机我们称之为社会动机，它们指的是人们的欲望，

sentences.en: to feel good about themselves as individuals and also feel good about themselves in terms of the groups that they belong to.
sentences.zh: 即作为个体对自己感觉良好，同时也对自己所属的群体感觉良好。

sentences.en: And I guess at the individual level, people like to feel, well, they like to feel, they like to have high self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 我想在个人层面上，人们喜欢感到，嗯，他们喜欢感到，他们喜欢拥有高自尊。

sentences.en: They like to feel good about themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢对自己感觉良好。

sentences.en: And potentially one way of doing that is to feel that you have access to information that other people don't necessarily have.
sentences.zh: 而实现这一点的一种潜在方式是，感觉自己拥有别人未必拥有的信息。

sentences.en: And this is quite a common rhetorical tool that people use when they talk about conspiracy theories, that everybody else is some kind of sheep, but that they know the truth, they
sentences.zh: 这是一种人们在谈论阴谋论时经常使用的修辞工具，即其他人都是某种“羊群”，但他们知道真相，他们

sentences.en: have the truth.
sentences.zh: 掌握了真相。

sentences.en: And having that kind of belief, I guess, feeling that you're in possession of information that other people don't have can give you a feeling of superiority over others.
sentences.zh: 拥有那种信念，我想，感觉自己掌握了别人没有的信息，可以让你产生一种对他人的优越感。

sentences.en: And we have found and others have shown as well that a need for uniqueness and a need to have, I guess, stand out from others is associated with belief in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，其他人也证明了，对独特性的需求和对，我想，从他人中脱颖而出的需求，与相信阴谋论有关。

sentences.en: And this happens at the level of the group as well.
sentences.zh: 这种情况也发生在群体层面。

sentences.en: So people who have an overinflated sense of the importance of the groups that they belong to, but at the same time, the feeling that those groups are underappreciated, those kinds
sentences.zh: 所以，那些对自己所属群体的重要性有过度膨胀感，但同时又觉得这些群体未被赏识的人，这些感觉

sentences.en: of feelings as well draw people towards conspiracy theories, especially conspiracy theories about their groups.
sentences.zh: 也会把人们推向阴谋论，尤其是关于他们群体的阴谋论。

sentences.en: So in having those sorts of beliefs, you can maintain the idea that your group is good and moral and upstanding, whereas others are the evildoers out there who are trying to ruin
sentences.zh: 因此，持有这些信念，你就可以维持这样一种观念：你的群体是善良、道德和正直的，而其他人则是那些试图毁掉

sentences.en: it for everybody else.
sentences.zh: 这一切的恶人。

sentences.en: So those three main motives, those three psychological motives, the epistemic, existential and social
sentences.zh: 所以这三个主要动机，这三个心理动机，认知、存在和社会动机，

sentences.en: is possible to summarize, I guess, the psychological literature on conspiracy theories into those three motivations.
sentences.zh: 我想，将关于阴谋论的心理学文献总结为这三个动机是可能的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's what we argue.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我们的观点。

sentences.en: What role, if any, does narcissism play in belief in conspiracy theories?
sentences.zh: 自恋在相信阴谋论中起什么作用（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: I mean, people who tend to be more narcissistic also believe in these theories as a means of getting that sort of the social capital?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些倾向于更自恋的人是否也相信这些理论，以此作为获得那种社会资本的手段？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 这是真的。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what I was referring to.
sentences.zh: 这正是我想表达的意思。

sentences.en: It's linked to the idea of need for uniqueness as well.
sentences.zh: 这也与对独特性的需求有关。

sentences.en: That's another, I guess, narcissistic notion that you have, you're in possession of information
sentences.zh: 这是另一种，我想，自恋的概念，即你拥有信息，

sentences.en: that other people don't have, you're different to other people and it makes you stand apart.
sentences.zh: 别人没有，你与众不同，这让你脱颖而出。

sentences.en: But yes, narcissism at an individual level has been associated in quite a few studies now with belief in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 但是是的，个人层面的自恋现在在相当多的研究中被发现与相信阴谋论有关。

sentences.en: And also this narcissism at the group level as well.
sentences.zh: 还有群体层面的这种自恋也是如此。

sentences.en: So an overinflated sense of the importance of your own group, that kind of insecure feeling about your own group is also associated with belief in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 因此，对自己群体重要性的过度膨胀感，以及对自己群体那种不安全感，也与相信阴谋论有关。

sentences.en: So yes, narcissism is one of those individual differences, variables that does correlate with belief in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，自恋是那些与相信阴谋论相关的个体差异变量之一。

sentences.en: So a few moments ago, you talked about education level as being a factor.
sentences.zh: 刚才你谈到了受教育程度是一个因素。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, what about other demographic categories such as age or gender?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，其他人口统计学类别，如年龄或性别呢？

sentences.en: Do you see any associations between those and tendency to believe in conspiracy theories?
sentences.zh: 你是否看到这些因素与相信阴谋论的倾向之间有任何关联？

sentences.en: Yes, in terms of age, we do.
sentences.zh: 是的，就年龄而言，我们确实看到了。

sentences.en: In our research, we generally find that older people believe in conspiracy theories less than younger people do.
sentences.zh: 在我们的研究中，我们通常发现老年人比年轻人更少相信阴谋论。

sentences.en: That tends to show up in most of the studies that we have run.
sentences.zh: 这在我们进行的大多数研究中往往都会体现出来。

sentences.en: So there's simply a correlation between conspiracy belief and age that is a negative correlation.
sentences.zh: 阴谋论信仰与年龄之间确实存在一种负相关关系。

sentences.en: So the more, the older you are, the less you believe in conspiracy theories or the other way around, the younger you are, the more you believe in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你年龄越大，就越不相信阴谋论；反之，你越年轻，就越相信阴谋论。

sentences.en: And that does tend to show up pretty much all of the time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况几乎在所有时候都会显现出来。

sentences.en: In terms of gender, we, at least in the research that myself and my colleagues have conducted,
sentences.zh: 至于性别，至少在我与同事所进行的研究中，

sentences.en: we've never found any differences in terms of gender differences in terms of conspiracy belief.
sentences.zh: 我们从未发现阴谋论信仰在性别上存在任何差异。

sentences.en: So as we measure belief in conspiracy theories using these psychological scales, we have never found that men believe more than women or women believe more than men or whatever.
sentences.zh: 当我们使用心理学量表来衡量对阴谋论的信仰时，我们从未发现男性比女性更相信，或者女性比男性更相信之类的情况。

sentences.en: We've never, we've never found anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我们从未发现过类似的情况。

sentences.en: I think one or two studies may have shown gender differences for specific conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 我想有一两项研究可能显示过针对特定阴谋论的性别差异。

sentences.en: Like I know of a recent study that, and I can't remember which direction it went in actually, but that showed that in terms of COVID-19 conspiracy theories,
sentences.zh: 比如我知道最近有一项研究，其实我不记得具体是哪种倾向了，但它显示在新冠肺炎阴谋论方面，

sentences.en: there was some kind of gender difference.
sentences.zh: 确实存在某种性别差异。

sentences.en: But personally, I've never found that, which I think is, is very interesting and kind of counterintuitive in a way,
sentences.zh: 但就我个人而言，我从未发现过这一点，我认为这非常有趣，而且在某种程度上有些反直觉，

sentences.en: because if people think about the prototypical conspiracy theorist, again, if you want to use that term to describe people, then they do tend to think of a, you know, middle aged,
sentences.zh: 因为如果人们想到典型的阴谋论者——再说一次，如果你想用这个词来描述这类人的话——他们确实倾向于想到一个，你知道，中年，

sentences.en: white man, usually.
sentences.zh: 白人男性，通常是这样。

sentences.en: And that may be the case for the prominent conspiracy theorists, you know, your well-known people who propagate these conspiracy theories,
sentences.zh: 对于那些著名的阴谋论者，也就是那些传播这些阴谋论的知名人士来说，情况可能确实如此，

sentences.en: but not necessarily your everyday person who's consuming this information on the internet and deciding whether or not it's true.
sentences.zh: 但并不一定适用于在互联网上消费这些信息并判断其真伪的普通人。

sentences.en: We don't really find those gender differences there.
sentences.zh: 我们在普通人群中并没有真正发现这些性别差异。

sentences.en: That's really interesting, I mean, because it is when you see, when we just had this, this overrun of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，我是说，因为当你看到，当我们刚刚经历了这次，这次对美国国会大厦的冲击，

sentences.en: Capitol here in Washington, and it looked like there were a lot of younger and middle aged men out there.
sentences.zh: 就在华盛顿这里，看起来外面有很多年轻人和中年男性。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly there were women involved, but, but that was the sense.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当然有女性参与其中，但，但这就是当时的感觉。

sentences.en: And of course, that is the conspiracy theory that the Trump election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 当然，那正是关于特朗普选举被窃取的阴谋论。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: I think, yeah, that's, that's extremely interesting.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，这，这极其有趣。

sentences.en: And of course, I was watching this on the news as well, and thinking very much the same thing.
sentences.zh: 当然，我当时也在新闻上看到了，想法也大同小异。

sentences.en: But I think that there probably is a difference in your, the person who sits at home and reads this information on the internet and decides whether or not it's true.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，坐在家里阅读互联网上的信息并判断其真伪的人，与那些真正准备去冲击大楼，

sentences.en: And the individuals who are prepared to actually go and storm a building or to go out and actively cause trouble based on these conspiracy beliefs.
sentences.zh: 或者基于这些阴谋论去主动制造麻烦的人之间，可能确实存在差异。

sentences.en: So there's, there's probably a lot going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这其中可能有很多复杂因素。

sentences.en: But in terms of the way we kind of measure belief in conspiracy theories, we just don't, with these sorts of gender differences that, that might seem obvious,
sentences.zh: 但就我们衡量阴谋论信仰的方式而言，我们只是没有发现那些看似显而易见的性别差异，

sentences.en: don't seem to play out really in, in the, in the research that we do on, on the everyday population, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 在我们在普通人群中所做的研究中，这些差异似乎并没有体现出来。

sentences.en: So another of your studies found that people who believe in one conspiracy theory are more likely to believe in others, even when those theories directly contradict each other.
sentences.zh: 那么，你的另一项研究发现，相信一种阴谋论的人更有可能相信其他阴谋论，即使这些理论直接相互矛盾。

sentences.en: So for instance, the more your participants believe that Princess Diana faked her own death, the more they also believe that she was murdered.
sentences.zh: 例如，参与者越相信戴安娜王妃伪造了自己的死亡，他们就越相信她是被人谋杀的。

sentences.en: And of course, that doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 当然，这完全说不通。

sentences.en: Can you help explain that?
sentences.zh: 你能帮忙解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 好的，当然。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We feel that that's a, that's, that is a very interesting finding, obviously.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是一个，一个非常有趣的发现，显而易见。

sentences.en: It, we kind of, I guess, started from the point that in the literature, it's often been found that if people believe in one conspiracy theory,
sentences.zh: 我们大概是从文献中经常发现的一点出发的，即如果人们相信一种阴谋论，

sentences.en: then they're likely to believe in others.
sentences.zh: 那么他们就很有可能相信其他阴谋论。

sentences.en: So, in other words, there's something that kind of holds these beliefs together.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，有什么东西将这些信仰联系在了一起。

sentences.en: So we were interested to find out, well, what is this, this underlying belief system or underlying attitude that might mean that these conspiracy beliefs are held at the same time,
sentences.zh: 所以我们很有兴趣找出，究竟是什么潜在的信仰体系或潜在态度，导致这些阴谋论可以同时被持有，

sentences.en: even if they, even if they do contradict one another.
sentences.zh: 即使它们，即使它们确实相互矛盾。

sentences.en: So we set to do these studies.
sentences.zh: 于是我们着手进行这些研究。

sentences.en: So we set to do these studies.
sentences.zh: 于是我们着手进行这些研究。

sentences.en: And so we asked participants in these studies to rate the extent to which they agree with different conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 我们要求这些研究的参与者对他们同意不同阴谋论的程度进行评分。

sentences.en: One, for example, that, um, Princess Diana was, was, um, assassinated by the royal family.
sentences.zh: 例如，其中一个，嗯，戴安娜王妃被，被，嗯，王室暗杀了。

sentences.en: Another one that she was, um, um, assassinated by MI5, nothing to do with the royal family.
sentences.zh: 另一个是她被，嗯，嗯，军情五处暗杀了，与王室无关。

sentences.en: Um, or others, um, also, but crucially, I think one that she was assassinated, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者其他的，嗯，但也至关重要的一点是，我认为其中一个说法是她被暗杀了，嗯，

sentences.en: and is dead and another that she was helped to fake her own death and that she's sort of living it up somewhere on, on an island, having a great time.
sentences.zh: 并且已经死了，而另一个说法是有人帮她伪造了死亡，她正在某个岛上过着逍遥自在的生活，玩得很开心。

sentences.en: So she's either, she, basically she, it's not possible to be dead and alive at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以她要么，她，基本上她，一个人不可能同时既死又活。

sentences.en: Unlike Schrodinger's cat.
sentences.zh: 不像薛定谔的猫。

sentences.en: And we also asked participants, yeah, well, that's, that's it.
sentences.zh: 我们也问了参与者，是的，嗯，就是这样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We thought it's just, we, we thought people would not entertain these two conspiracy theories at the same time, but it turned out that they did.
sentences.zh: 我们原以为人们不会同时持有这两种阴谋论，但事实证明他们确实持有。

sentences.en: Um, or at least they were prepared to entertain the idea that both of those things might be true, but we also measured the extent to which people believed in, I guess,
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者至少他们愿意接受这两种说法可能都是真的想法，但我们也衡量了人们在多大程度上相信，我猜，

sentences.en: an underlying conspiracy theory that something just isn't right.
sentences.zh: 一种潜在的阴谋论，即有些事情就是不对劲。

sentences.en: Something, something's up and something is being covered up.
sentences.zh: 有些事情，有些事情发生了，而且有些事情正在被掩盖。

sentences.en: And what we found was that, um, people did indeed endorse these contradictory conspiracy theories or again, at least be, um,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，嗯，人们确实支持这些相互矛盾的阴谋论，或者再说一次，至少，嗯，

sentences.en: were likely to entertain those two ideas at the same time.
sentences.zh: 很乐意同时接受这两种想法。

sentences.en: But once we also took into account the extent to which they believed that there was just something up, then that relationship actually disappeared.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们考虑到他们认为“有些事情不对劲”的程度，这种关系实际上就消失了。

sentences.en: So it was the relationship between the contradictory beliefs was explained by the, I guess, underlying belief that just something is being covered up.
sentences.zh: 所以，矛盾信仰之间的关系是由，我猜，那种“有些事情正在被掩盖”的潜在信仰所解释的。

sentences.en: So you can explain why people will entertain these contradictory ideas,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以解释为什么人们会接受这些相互矛盾的想法，

sentences.en: because both of those ideas are consistent with the underlying idea that there's just something not quite right.
sentences.zh: 因为这两种想法都与“有些事情不太对劲”这一潜在观念相一致。

sentences.en: So it's not necessarily to say that they will definitely believe that Princess Diana is dead and at the same time believe that she's still alive,
sentences.zh: 所以这并不一定意味着他们会坚定地相信戴安娜王妃已经死了，同时又相信她还活着，

sentences.en: but they'll be happy to entertain the idea that those two things are possible as long as they also entertain the belief that there was just something that wasn't right about those events.
sentences.zh: 但只要他们同时也持有“这些事件中有些事情不对劲”的信念，他们就会很乐意接受这两种情况都有可能发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That helps explain it at least a little bit.
sentences.zh: 这至少在一定程度上解释了这个问题。

sentences.en: Well, what makes a conspiracy theory catch on and have staying power?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让一个阴谋论流行起来并具有持久力呢？

sentences.en: Are there certain types of theories that are stickier than others or, or some that are more enduring?
sentences.zh: 是否有些类型的理论比其他理论更具粘性，或者有些理论更持久？

sentences.en: Like the earth is flat and has been around since forever.
sentences.zh: 比如“地球是平的”这种说法，它一直存在。

sentences.en: You know, so are, are there characteristics that, that, uh, make them stickier?
sentences.zh: 你知道，那么，有没有什么特征，让它们更具粘性？

sentences.en: Um, it's, that's not something that I've done research on myself, to be honest, but I think it's a fascinating question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，老实说，这不是我亲自研究过的课题，但我认为这是一个引人入胜的问题。

sentences.en: Um, it's very true that some conspiracy theories stand the test of time and others just disappear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实有些阴谋论经受住了时间的考验，而另一些则消失了。

sentences.en: I think that, um, so there must be certain features of conspiracy theories, the ones that last and the ones that don't, I don't personally know exactly what they are.
sentences.zh: 我认为，嗯，所以阴谋论一定有一些特定的特征，那些能持续下去的和不能持续下去的，我个人并不确切知道它们是什么。

sentences.en: But, um, I, I guess one thing that tends to be very, very common is that the event is very, very large.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，我，我猜一个非常非常普遍的特征是，该事件非常非常重大。

sentences.en: The event that is explained by the conspiracy theory is very, very large and important and usually involving something of great political or social significance.
sentences.zh: 阴谋论所解释的事件非常非常重大且重要，通常涉及具有重大政治或社会意义的事情。

sentences.en: Um, a lot of other conspiracy theories that you might come across just sort of disappear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能遇到的许多其他阴谋论只是消失了。

sentences.en: And I guess a lot of the time we just don't really know why they don't, they don't catch on.
sentences.zh: 我想很多时候我们真的不知道为什么它们没有，它们没有流行起来。

sentences.en: Um, but, um, but plenty of them, plenty of them do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，嗯，但是有很多，有很多确实流行起来了。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, it's an, it's a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: It's a line of research for you to pursue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个值得你去深入研究的研究方向。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: This there, there definitely is.
sentences.zh: 这，这绝对是有的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, I think that other researchers have started to ask these sorts of questions, but, and I have tried myself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为其他研究人员已经开始提出这类问题了，但我自己也尝试过。

sentences.en: I guess, um, not taxonomized, but sort of almost, I guess, not, not even categorized conspiracy theories, but try to try to isolate some of these features.
sentences.zh: 我猜，嗯，不是分类，而是几乎，我猜，甚至不是，不是对阴谋论进行分类，而是试图试图分离出其中的一些特征。

sentences.en: But it's actually very difficult because there are so many of them about so many different events.
sentences.zh: 但这实际上非常困难，因为关于这么多不同的事件，有太多的阴谋论了。

sentences.en: And you pointed out the, um, flat earth conspiracy theory, which has been around forever, but, um, kind of died away for a long time.
sentences.zh: 你指出了“地平说”阴谋论，它一直存在，但，嗯，在很长一段时间里几乎销声匿迹了。

sentences.en: And then in recent years just seems to have gotten popular again.
sentences.zh: 然后在最近几年似乎又变得流行起来。

sentences.en: Um, and I, I do find it quite difficult to explain that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实觉得很难解释这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, I have, I, I have a theory about that conspiracy theory that just generally people are becoming less trustful of science and scientists at the present time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我，我有一个关于那个阴谋论的理论，即人们普遍对科学和科学家变得越来越不信任。

sentences.en: Um, which is why we might be seeing these sorts of ideas, making a bit of a comeback, but, um, yeah, no, it's, I think it's, it's a really, really fascinating question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么我们可能会看到这些想法卷土重来，但是，嗯，是的，不，我认为这是一个非常非常引人入胜的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it's not that even they, some of them disappear, they, they go away, but then they come, they come back again, um,
sentences.zh: 因为并不是说它们消失了，它们离开了，然后它们又回来了，嗯，

sentences.en: or come back again in a different form or certain conspiracy theories, um, about, uh, particular things like say anti,
sentences.zh: 或者以不同的形式卷土重来，或者某些阴谋论，嗯，关于，呃，特定的事情，比如，反，

sentences.en: anti vaccine or health related conspiracy theories can kind of reinvent themselves for, uh, new things that happen.
sentences.zh: 反疫苗或与健康相关的阴谋论，可以为，呃，发生的新事物进行自我重塑。

sentences.en: Like 5g conspiracy theories about, um, people getting sick from, um, foreign masks and things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如关于5G的阴谋论，关于，嗯，人们因为，嗯，外国口罩之类的东西而生病。

sentences.en: So there, there, these sorts of conspiracy theories have always been there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些阴谋论一直都在那里。

sentences.en: They kind of mutate, I suppose, if you like, they change.
sentences.zh: 它们会变异，我想，如果你愿意这么说的话，它们会改变。

sentences.en: Um, but yeah, I think it is a really fascinating question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是是的，我认为这确实是一个非常引人入胜的问题。

sentences.en: And one that I can't, as a social psychologist, can't really answer very well, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，作为一个社会心理学家，我无法很好地回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Is there any way to, to effectively debunk a conspiracy theory once it's out there?
sentences.zh: 一旦阴谋论传播开来，有什么方法可以有效地揭穿它吗？

sentences.en: I mean, can you just present the facts?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能直接摆出事实吗？

sentences.en: Like you talked about, um, the anti-vaxxers, um, you know, the fact that the, the Lancet article that kind of led to a lot of beliefs that, um, children were, were, um,
sentences.zh: 就像你提到的，嗯，反疫苗者，嗯，你知道，那篇《柳叶刀》文章导致了许多人相信，嗯，儿童，嗯，

sentences.en: becoming autistic as a result of, of vaccines.
sentences.zh: 因为疫苗而患上自闭症。

sentences.en: And then it turned out that that, that article was, was bogus.
sentences.zh: 后来事实证明，那篇文章是伪造的。

sentences.en: It was, it was based on faulty data and it was retracted.
sentences.zh: 它是基于错误的数据，并且被撤回了。

sentences.en: And yet some people are still hanging onto that.
sentences.zh: 然而有些人仍然坚持这种观点。

sentences.en: So is there a way to, to stop these theories from, from continuing to swirl?
sentences.zh: 那么有什么方法可以阻止这些理论继续流传吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there, there are ways to do this, but of course it's extremely challenging.
sentences.zh: 是的，有方法可以做到这一点，但当然这极具挑战性。

sentences.en: It's very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这非常非常困难。

sentences.en: Once, once these conspiracy theories are out there and people believe them,
sentences.zh: 一旦，一旦这些阴谋论传播开来，人们相信了它们，

sentences.en: then sometimes people can very, very strongly hold on to these beliefs and defend them, um, very, very strongly as well.
sentences.zh: 那么有时人们会非常非常强烈地坚持这些信念，并且也会非常非常强烈地捍卫它们。

sentences.en: And once these attitudes are very, very strong, of course, um, from other areas of psychology,
sentences.zh: 一旦这些态度变得非常非常强烈，当然，嗯，从心理学的其他领域来看，

sentences.en: we know that attitudes that are very strongly held are difficult to, um, dispute, I guess, difficult to, difficult to change.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，根深蒂固的态度很难，嗯，反驳，我猜，很难，很难改变。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to change these sorts of attitudes.
sentences.zh: 改变这类态度非常困难。

sentences.en: Um, and so, yes, it is a challenge, but there are things that, that can be done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，是的，这是一个挑战，但确实有一些事情是可以做的。

sentences.en: And, um, a lot of research that, especially in, in very, very recent years as well, has started to come out, um, in terms of how do you, how do you address misinformation?
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，很多研究，特别是在，在最近几年，已经开始出现，嗯，关于你如何，你如何应对错误信息？

sentences.en: How do you address conspiracy theories?
sentences.zh: 你如何应对阴谋论？

sentences.en: And giving people the facts does work, um, under certain, under certain situations.
sentences.zh: 在某些，在某些情况下，给人们提供事实确实有效。

sentences.en: In some of our own research, we've actually found that, um, it's, uh, quite effective to provide people with factual information, provide people with the facts.
sentences.zh: 在我们自己的一些研究中，我们实际上发现，嗯，给人们提供事实信息，给人们提供事实，是相当有效的。

sentences.en: And this is, this was particularly about vaccines, um, before they're exposed to conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 这特别是在疫苗方面，嗯，在他们接触阴谋论之前。

sentences.en: And then the conspiracy theory sort of fails to gain traction.
sentences.zh: 然后阴谋论就无法获得关注了。

sentences.en: But once the people have been exposed to the conspiracy theory, then giving them misinformation, giving them the, I guess, sorry,
sentences.zh: 但一旦人们接触了阴谋论，那么给他们错误信息，给他们，我猜，抱歉，

sentences.en: the appropriate or correct information afterwards doesn't really work.
sentences.zh: 事后给他们提供适当或正确的信息其实并不起作用。

sentences.en: So, um,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，

sentences.en: others have sort of taken this information and have started to look at ways to inoculate people against misinformation and to inoculate people against conspiracy theories and fake news and all sorts of other things,
sentences.zh: 其他人已经采纳了这些信息，并开始研究如何让人们对错误信息产生免疫，以及如何让人们对阴谋论、假新闻和各种其他事物产生免疫，

sentences.en: um, which seems to be working as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这似乎也行得通。

sentences.en: So, uh, in other words, you give people either the correct information or some piece of weak misinformation before they're exposed to the worst of it,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，换句话说，你在人们接触到最糟糕的信息之前，给他们提供正确的信息或一些微弱的错误信息，

sentences.en: then that helps them to be able to resist it.
sentences.zh: 那么这有助于他们能够抵御它。

sentences.en: Um, there are other techniques that people have used that researchers have used as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有其他人使用过的其他技术，研究人员也使用过。

sentences.en: And, um, just to give you one other example,
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，再给你举一个例子，

sentences.en: some researchers have looked at the idea of presenting people with a pre warning or a forewarning that they might be exposed to misinformation.
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员研究了向人们发出预警或提前警告他们可能会接触到错误信息的想法。

sentences.en: And if people believe that information that they might receive could be misleading and they have that information upfront,
sentences.zh: 如果人们认为他们可能收到的信息具有误导性，并且他们提前获得了这些信息，

sentences.en: then that can sometimes help them to resist the misinformation as well.
sentences.zh: 那么这有时也能帮助他们抵御错误信息。

sentences.en: Now, I think these, these are all really, really valuable tools, but of course, um, sometimes the misinformation is already out there.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为这些，这些都是非常有价值的工具，但当然，嗯，有时错误信息已经传播开了。

sentences.en: Um, so it's difficult to get to people beforehand.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以很难提前接触到人们。

sentences.en: So then you have to resort to, I guess, traditional debunking techniques, such as going in with consistent, strong, um, counter arguments.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须诉诸，我猜，传统的揭穿技术，比如用一致、强有力的反驳论点去应对。

sentences.en: But I think that these other opportunities, these other, um,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些其他机会，这些其他，嗯，

sentences.en: techniques provide real opportunities to help people to resist conspiracy theories in general that they might come across in the future.
sentences.zh: 技术提供了真正的机会，帮助人们抵御未来可能遇到的阴谋论。

sentences.en: So if you give people these sorts of, I guess, ways to critically think about information and, um, and think, well, you know, okay, I could be exposed to misinformation.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你给人们这些，我猜，批判性思考信息的方式，嗯，并且思考，好吧，你知道，我可以接触到错误信息。

sentences.en: That misinformation is out there, so I'm going to be on the lookout for it, then it might actually help people to resist it when they come across it next time, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 那些错误信息就在那里，所以我得提防着点，那么这实际上可能有助于人们在下次遇到时抵御它，如果这说得通的话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds like the techniques that they're trying to use right now with the COVID-19 vaccines, you know, telling people upfront that, you know,
sentences.zh: 这听起来就像他们现在试图在新冠疫苗上使用的技术，你知道，提前告诉人们，你知道，

sentences.en: if you happen to be particularly allergic, you might have a reaction.
sentences.zh: 如果你恰好特别过敏，你可能会有反应。

sentences.en: This is what to expect.
sentences.zh: 这就是预期的结果。

sentences.en: And yet it's kind of like a game of whack-a-mole because they talk about all of this and they're trying to be as transparent as possible.
sentences.zh: 然而这就像一场打地鼠游戏，因为他们谈论了所有这些，并且试图尽可能保持透明。

sentences.en: And yet along comes somebody who says that the MRNA that's involved in this is actually going to change the DNA in your body.
sentences.zh: 然而，总有人跳出来说，其中涉及的mRNA实际上会改变你体内的DNA。

sentences.en: And so, you know, how do you fight that?
sentences.zh: 那么，你知道，你该如何反击呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very, very, it is very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: And there are new conspiracy theories all the time.
sentences.zh: 而且新的阴谋论层出不穷。

sentences.en: It's, it is, it is exactly like that game.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像那个游戏一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're constantly trying to, you've got one and then you'd constantly trying to hit another one away.
sentences.zh: 你一直在努力，刚解决一个，就得不断地去对付下一个。

sentences.en: It's, it is very, very challenging.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有挑战性。

sentences.en: It's, it's, there's a lot, there's a lot out there, a lot going on out there.
sentences.zh: 确实，外界有很多信息，发生了很多事情。

sentences.en: And of course, this is all complicated by the fact that sometimes conspiracies do exiSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，这一切因为有时阴谋论确实存在而变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: And sometimes people may have deep seated valid reasons to distrust authority.
sentences.zh: 有时人们对权威的不信任确实有根深蒂固的合理理由。

sentences.en: So for example,
sentences.zh: 比如，

sentences.en: public opinion polls have found that black Americans are less likely to say they'll take the COVID vaccine and more wary of its safety because they have a long history of being abused and mistreated by the medical establishment.
sentences.zh: 民意调查发现，美国黑人不太愿意接种新冠疫苗，对疫苗的安全性也更为警惕，因为他们有着长期被医疗机构虐待和不公正对待的历史。

sentences.en: So is there a way for people to balance this awareness with a healthy skepticism of conspiracy theories?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们有没有办法在保持这种认知的同时，对阴谋论保持一种健康的怀疑态度呢？

sentences.en: Yes, again, this is extremely challenging and you're absolutely right that some people have very good reasons to be suspicious of, of,
sentences.zh: 是的，这同样极具挑战性。你说得完全正确，有些人因为过去发生的事件，对这类事情持怀疑态度是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: of these sorts of things because of past events.
sentences.zh: 因为过去发生的那些事。

sentences.en: And, and so the challenge becomes even greater.
sentences.zh: 所以，挑战变得更加艰巨了。

sentences.en: And so, and I don't know the solution to this, apart from the fact that people who are attempting to fight the misinformation will need to be sensitive to these concerns and,
sentences.zh: 我不知道解决办法，除了那些试图打击虚假信息的人需要对这些顾虑保持敏感，

sentences.en: and perhaps be more targeted in their efforts to debunk the misinformation, being sensitive to these, these historical events as well.
sentences.zh: 并且在揭穿虚假信息时采取更有针对性的策略，同时也要对这些历史事件保持敏感。

sentences.en: Um, so it can't necessarily be a one size fits all approach to misinformation just can't be because everybody's circumstances are different.
sentences.zh: 所以，针对虚假信息未必能采取“一刀切”的方法，因为每个人的情况都不同。

sentences.en: And we know that different communities feel differently about vaccines, um, and various other things as well for very good reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，不同的群体出于非常正当的理由，对疫苗以及其他各种事物的看法也各不相同。

sentences.en: So, um, so, um, that of course is a huge challenge for anybody trying to deal with, um, potential misinformation about vaccines and, and, and other things, but also, yeah,
sentences.zh: 所以，这对任何试图处理有关疫苗及其他潜在虚假信息的人来说，当然是一个巨大的挑战，而且，

sentences.en: particularly with COVID a reluctance to, to take the vaccine.
sentences.zh: 特别是在新冠疫情期间，人们对接种疫苗存在抵触情绪。

sentences.en: So what aspects of conspiracy theory are you looking at today?
sentences.zh: 那么，你今天关注的是阴谋论的哪些方面呢？

sentences.en: What, what's your research, um, heading toward?
sentences.zh: 你的研究方向是什么？

sentences.en: Um, uh, quite a few things going on at the moment, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实目前正在进行的研究还挺多的。

sentences.en: Um, I'm really interested in, um, I guess the deliberate use of conspiracy theories as a, as a political, um, device.
sentences.zh: 我非常感兴趣的是，人们如何将阴谋论作为一种政治手段来刻意使用。

sentences.en: So I've been doing some research, um, I guess,
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在做一些研究，

sentences.en: looking at how people perceive others who are seen to use conspiracy theories and whether or not they see those actions as intentional or deliberate.
sentences.zh: 观察人们如何看待那些被认为在使用阴谋论的人，以及他们是否认为这些行为是有意或蓄意的。

sentences.en: Um, um, and also what the effects are of, of that.
sentences.zh: 还有，这些行为会产生什么影响。

sentences.en: Um, I've also been interested in the term conspiracy theory itself and the term conspiracy theorist and how people use those terms, um, whether they use them to, uh, I guess,
sentences.zh: 我也一直对“阴谋论”和“阴谋论者”这两个词本身很感兴趣，以及人们是如何使用这些词的，他们是否用这些词来，

sentences.en: specifically, um, put down other people's ideas.
sentences.zh: 专门贬低他人的观点。

sentences.en: Um, or if they simply use these terms when people,
sentences.zh: 或者，当人们仅仅是不相信某个特定观点时，是否也会使用这些词，以及这些词对某人是否会真正相信某事有什么影响。

sentences.en: when they just don't believe that they don't believe a particular idea and also the effects of these terms on whether or not someone will actually believe something.
sentences.zh: 我还做了些什么呢？

sentences.en: Um, what else have I been doing?
sentences.zh: 哦，确实有很多事情在进行。

sentences.en: Oh, quite a, you know, quite a few things going on.
sentences.zh: 我写了不少关于新冠疫情阴谋论的文章。

sentences.en: I've been writing quite a bit about COVID-19 conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 而且，总的来说，我的研究很大程度上也集中在相信阴谋论所带来的后果上。

sentences.en: And in, in also quite generally, my research is, is focused a lot on the consequences of believing in conspiracy theories as well.
sentences.zh: 在不同的领域，比如疫苗、气候变化、政治等各个方面，具体来说，阴谋论对人们的态度、信念和行为有什么影响。

sentences.en: So in different, um, areas like in vaccines, climate change, um, politics in various different domains, specifically what impact do,
sentences.zh: 所以我在这方面做了很多工作。

sentences.en: do conspiracy theories have on people's attitudes, um, beliefs and behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常值得深入研究的领域，非常感谢你所做的工作，帮助我们更好地理解人们的思维方式。

sentences.en: So I've been doing a lot on that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天能参加我们的节目，道格拉斯博士。

sentences.en: Well, it's an amazing area for, uh, scrutiny and, and appreciate the work that you're doing here and helping us to better understand, uh, some of the ways that, uh,
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: people's minds work.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来这里。
